### Season outlook as written in the guide (p. 284)

After missing out on the College Football Playoff in his first season at the helm, Kalen DeBoer led Alabama to the CFP in 2025. The Crimson Tide were a flawed, one-dimensional offense but managed to dispatch the Sooners before the eventual national champion Hoosiers sent them packing. In Tuscaloosa, that is a disappointing season. DeBoer must now rebuild the offense after numerous departures, including first-round selection Ty Simpson. Alabama has a young, high-upside quarterback potentially ready to replace him, but can DeBoer meet the lofty expectations set by a rabid fanbase? If everything clicks on offense, this is a Crimson Tide team that has the pieces to bring home its first national title of the DeBoer era. Over 8.5 The belief in Alabama rests solely on the shoulders of Russell. Given DeBoer’s track record of developing quarterbacks, it’s a safe bet that Russell will be what most expect him to be. His athleticism should also help turn around an offense that really struggled to run the ball last year. So too should the investments in the offensive line. Defensively, this unit should be just as productive as it was, with seven starters back. The Tide have an extremely favorable schedule as well. They avoid Texas and Ole Miss. Alabama must face both Georgia and Texas A&M, but it gets to host both. The toughest road trip in conference will be to LSU in November. Oddly enough, it seems the Crimson Tide, of all programs, is flying under the radar. Bettors should invest early — not only in a win total, but in conference odds and national championship odds.

## 26. Open Questions / Risks

The guide's *Three Burning Questions for the 2026 Season* *(p. 285)*, with the answers as written:

### Who takes over for Ty Simpson at quarterback?

The expectation is that redshirt freshman Keelon Russell will be the starter for Alabama this season, but DeBoer will have a “competition” for the job when fall camp begins. Russell adds an athletic dynamic to the position that Simpson did not, and it is one of many reasons why many expect him to win the job. Russell also fits the RPO offense that DeBoer and offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb want to run. The Tide finished 31st in EPA per play through the air and 21st in success rate when dropping back. Whether it is Russell or senior Austin Mack, both will likely be less efficient than Simpson was a season ago. Bettors can expect more production on the ground from the position, though.

### Can Alabama find its rushing attack once again?

There was an immense load on the passing attack’s shoulders last year because Alabama could not run the ball. The Crimson Tide averaged just 3.4 yards per carry and 104 rush yards per game. They finished 132nd in rush success rate (34.5%), placed in the 18th percentile in rush EPA per play and in the sixth percentile in explosive run rate. Leading rusher Jam Miller (520 yards) is gone, and so too are six offensive linemen who started games. Sophomore Michael Carroll — who will start at either right guard or tackle — is the lone returnee. Perhaps that is a good thing for such an anemic rush offense. Either way, finding some semblance of balance with this unit needs to be a priority this season.

### Is this team a national championship contender?

If Russell wins the job and is everything most expect, the answer is yes. Many of the questions with the Tide are on the offensive side of the ball. On defense, seven starters are back from one of the better units in college football. The Tide finished 29th in opponent EPA per play and 25th in success rate. In fact, the defense got somewhat unlucky last season, ranking in the 91st percentile in early-down EPA per play but the 51st percentile in late-down success rate. Alabama’s secondary is one of the best in the country, with three starters back and five-star freshman Jorden Edmonds now in the mix. The Tide have what they need on defense. If the offense hits, this team should be able to romp through a manageable schedule and into the College Football Playoff.
